_comment: DENY-SIDE BACKSTOP for the zebra vetting agents. Tracked in git.
Read this before adding anything to an 'allow' list here: measured on
2026-08-12, a project settings.json ALLOW rule is IGNORED by `claude -p`.
Claude Code will not grant itself permissions from a file sitting in its
working directory — otherwise cloning a repo would hand it capabilities.
DENY rules from this file ARE honoured.
So the grants live on the spawn command line instead: zebra/config.py
VET_ALLOWED_TOOLS -> `--allowedTools`, verified end-to-end by having a
real spawned agent run `zebra vet show` and return the right answer.
This file is the second layer, and it is the one that matters most: it
still applies when a human runs `claude` interactively on the Pi, where
no --disallowedTools flag is in play.
THE INVARIANT: no agent, spawned or interactive, may open or close a
position. Verified 2026-08-12 by asking a real agent to run
`zebra close --help` (harmless even if the deny failed) — it answered
DENIED. Do not weaken these patterns; the wildcards are what make them
survive a `cd foo && python -m zebra close` phrasing.
2026-08-13: the five position verbs were NOT the whole invariant. The
cycle verbs call them. `zebra run` opens positions (_enter_as_bcs),
closes them (_paper_auto_close) and recursively spawns more agents; it
was granted by the coarse allow rule and denied here by nothing. `loop`
is the same cycle held open, `scan` mutates the watchlist, `report`
Telegrams the owner. Deny the callers, not just the callees.
2026-08-13 (later): the same test applied to the verbs added since found
`postmortem run`, which calls spawn_batch -> _spawn_generic, so it is a
SPAWNER — the very class the paragraph above exists to catch — and it was
reachable by every channel. Denied here and on argv; no channel needs it.
2026-08-14, REVERTED SAME DAY: `events replace` was added here too, and
that was a MISTAKE that broke the calendar refresher. This file's deny
applies to EVERY spawned agent, and the per-channel carve-out in
vet._denied_tools only edits the argv --disallowedTools list — it cannot
grant back something denied here. So the events channel, whose entire job
is installing the calendar, was denied the one verb it exists to run.
THE RULE THIS FILE NOW ENCODES: a deny that must vary BY CHANNEL cannot
live in this file. This file is all-or-nothing, and its real job is the
human-interactive backstop where no argv flags are in play. Per-channel
scoping belongs in VET_DENIED_TOOLS + vet._denied_tools ONLY. Adding a
per-channel rule here silently disables the channel that needs it, and
the failure looks exactly like an auth error from the outside.
